title: Governing principles
summary: The owner's rules that settle design questions everywhere in the app.
description: The owner's rules. When a change is unclear, or two parts of the app disagree, these decide. They change only on the owner's word.

stories.want: design questions settled by a few rules that hold everywhere
stories.soThat: the app stays one thing as it grows

stories.want: what I have earned and made to stay mine
stories.soThat: I can trust the app with my effort

requirements.text: A course is made for what the learner asks for; the app never decides what is worth learning.
A level (CEFR, A1 to C2) describes material and never limits what can be made or practised: a request at any level is made as asked.
Nothing the tutor makes waits for approval: keeping it is approving it, deleting it is rejecting it.

The app does not fill in the learner's existing content by itself at startup. When a new feature needs something existing content lacks, a button asks the tutor to add it, in a conversation the learner can read.
A course can be finished regardless of time: passing a lesson again the same day always adds mastery points, and no step toward mastery requires waiting for a check-in to come due.
Mastery is never lost: a mastered lesson stays mastered whatever its later results.

history.text: Mastery is never lost through practice: a mastered lesson stays mastered whatever its later results. Only the learner's own reset of progress clears it.
history.reason: Reset progress, the one thing that cleared mastery, was removed.

requirements.text: Closing a mastered course is final: nothing is added to it, changed in it or brought back from it.
A mastered subject is revisited through a new course from the tutor, never by reopening the old one.
Today's lessons are a short way in, not a backlog: what is due never piles up on the home screen.
A lesson that fits no course goes in the single folder `term.other-lessons`.
For each song and podcast, enough is kept to rebuild the exact prompt that made it.
A lesson type is declared in one place, and the screens and the lesson flow ask the type instead of branching on it.
Every row that names a thing (a course, a lesson, a word, a song, a memory) has a tagged id that says what it is; screens show the title of the thing instead of the id.
